cond_0001.intro: We are looking for someone to join our team in this role.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Responsible for overseeing the day-to-day activities of assigned laboratory functions. Responsible for the accurate and timely performance of complex quantitative and/or qualitative analyses. Process and screen cytological specimens from various body sites. Work in close relationship with Pathologists in review and interpretation of the specimens. Recognize abnormal and normal cells and classify findings.
CORE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Coordinate the testing activities of the cytology department, oversee staff involved in the technical preparation of gynecological and non-gynecological samples for cytological review.
Assist in developing, reviewing, recommending, laboratory procedures, policies, and systems.
Assist with the evaluation of competency of testing personnel. Identify testing personnel training needs and ensure training & education are received as appropriate for lab responsibilities.
Perform and analyze according to SOP, basic and complex diagnostic procedures designed to produce accurate reproducible results to meet the needs of patients, as requested by the physician.
Assist Physicians with FNA specimen adequacy determination during patient procedures.
Prepare, reagent, and solution correctly and accurately to complete necessary testing/requests according to the SOP.
Restock the work area and FNA carts of needed supplies to assist co-workers in the performance of their duties.
Prepare and accession patient specimens, accepting only patient specimens for testing that are properly collected and labeled. Evaluate sufficiency of patient information given with specimens and resolve issues with specimen collection and specimen orders in accordance with established laboratory policies.
Perform required quality assurance and control procedures on a predetermined schedule to ascertain the reliability of reagents and laboratory equipment/instrumentation resulting in timely accurate reproducible test results to ensure quality patient care and complete quality control records legibly and accurately.
Perform required troubleshooting and subsequent appropriate problem resolution, in a timely manner (e.g., review of the QC records).
Participate, as required, in proficiency testing/interpretation/reporting using established procedures and resulting in a satisfactory report.
Promptly verify, abnormal/panic results and notifies, as required per SOP, patient care unit and/or physician with full documentation of steps taken.
Participate in the educational endeavors of the institution to meet the current and future needs of the hospital.
Participate, as required, in the training, supervision and evaluation of new employees, as established by laboratory policies (e.g., section training checklist).
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Able to stand and/or sit for long periods of time.
Visual acuity must not be impaired. Color differentiation is required.
Manual dexterity for instrument operation including microscope.
WORKING ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Noisy environment.
Foul or unpleasant odors.
Perform procedures and operate instrumentation while wearing protective apparel.
May be exposed to virus, disease, and infection from patients and specimens.
SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
Able to use a computer keyboard, monitor and mouse.
Able to communicate verbally, written and electronically with healthcare personnel, families and patients.
Able to use numerous types of laboratory equipment.
Ability to organize and prioritize time and tasks to achieve a well-coordinated work effort and to effectively meet work schedules and deadlines.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Certified by American Society of Clinical Pathologist (ASCP) or equivalent agency as a Cytotechnologist.
Five (5) years' experience as a Cytotechnologist.
Preferred Requirements
Licensed by the state of [Location masked] within 6 months of employment.

cond_0022.intro: We are looking for someone to join our team in this role. Responsible for overseeing the day-to-day activities of assigned laboratory functions. Responsible for the accurate and timely performance of complex quantitative and/or qualitative analyses. Process and screen cytological specimens from various body sites. Work in close relationship with Pathologists in review and interpretation of the specimens. Recognize abnormal and normal cells and classify findings. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of cytological analysis and specimen interpretation.
cond_0022.responsibilities:
CORE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Coordinate the testing activities of the cytology department, oversee staff involved in the technical preparation of gynecological and non-gynecological samples for cytological review.
Assist in developing, reviewing, recommending, laboratory procedures, policies, and systems.
Assist with the evaluation of competency of testing personnel. Identify testing personnel training needs and ensure training & education are received as appropriate for lab responsibilities.
Perform and analyze according to SOP, basic and complex diagnostic procedures designed to produce accurate reproducible results to meet the needs of patients, as requested by the physician.
Assist Physicians with FNA specimen adequacy determination during patient procedures.
Prepare, reagent, and solution correctly and accurately to complete necessary testing/requests according to the SOP.
Restock the work area and FNA carts of needed supplies to assist co-workers in the performance of their duties.
Prepare and accession patient specimens, accepting only patient specimens for testing that are properly collected and labeled. Evaluate sufficiency of patient information given with specimens and resolve issues with specimen collection and specimen orders in accordance with established laboratory policies.
Perform required quality assurance and control procedures on a predetermined schedule to ascertain the reliability of reagents and laboratory equipment/instrumentation resulting in timely accurate reproducible test results to ensure quality patient care and complete quality control records legibly and accurately.
Perform required troubleshooting and subsequent appropriate problem resolution, in a timely manner (e.g., review of the QC records).
Participate, as required, in proficiency testing/interpretation/reporting using established procedures and resulting in a satisfactory report.
Promptly verify, abnormal/panic results and notifies, as required per SOP, patient care unit and/or physician with full documentation of steps taken.
Participate in the educational endeavors of the institution to meet the current and future needs of the hospital.
Participate, as required, in the training, supervision and evaluation of new employees, as established by laboratory policies (e.g., section training checklist).
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Able to stand and/or sit for long periods of time.
Visual acuity must not be impaired. Color differentiation is required.
Manual dexterity for instrument operation including microscope.
WORKING ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Noisy environment.
Foul or unpleasant odors.
Perform procedures and operate instrumentation while wearing protective apparel.
May be exposed to virus, disease, and infection from patients and specimens.
SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
Able to use a computer keyboard, monitor and mouse.
Able to communicate verbally, written and electronically with healthcare personnel, families and patients.
Able to use numerous types of laboratory equipment.
Ability to organize and prioritize time and tasks to achieve a well-coordinated work effort and to effectively meet work schedules and deadlines.

This role works closely with Pathologists and laboratory staff to support accurate and timely performance of complex cytological analyses, including processing and screening specimens from various body sites, and contributing to the review and interpretation of findings.

Collaborate on developing, reviewing, and recommending laboratory procedures, policies, and systems.
Support the evaluation of competency of testing personnel. Help identify training needs and ensure training and education are received as appropriate for lab responsibilities.
Perform and analyze according to SOP, basic and complex diagnostic procedures designed to produce accurate reproducible results to meet the needs of patients, as requested by the physician.

This role works closely with Pathologists and laboratory staff to support accurate and timely performance of complex cytological analyses, including processing and screening specimens from various body sites, and contributing to the review and interpretation of findings.
cond_0189.responsibilities:
CORE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Coordinate the testing activities of the cytology department, working alongside staff involved in the technical preparation of gynecological and non-gynecological samples for cytological review.
Collaborate in developing, reviewing, and recommending laboratory procedures, policies, and systems.
Support the evaluation of competency of testing personnel. Help identify training needs and ensure staff receive appropriate training and education for their lab responsibilities.
Perform and analyze according to SOP, basic and complex diagnostic procedures designed to produce accurate reproducible results to meet the needs of patients, as requested by the physician.
Work alongside Physicians to assist with FNA specimen adequacy determination during patient procedures.
Prepare reagents and solutions correctly and accurately to complete necessary testing/requests according to the SOP.
Restock the work area and FNA carts of needed supplies to assist co-workers in the performance of their duties.
Prepare and accession patient specimens, accepting only patient specimens for testing that are properly collected and labeled. Evaluate sufficiency of patient information given with specimens and help resolve issues with specimen collection and specimen orders in accordance with established laboratory policies.
Carry out required quality assurance and control procedures on a predetermined schedule to support the reliability of reagents and laboratory equipment/instrumentation, and complete quality control records legibly and accurately.
Perform required troubleshooting and coordinate appropriate problem resolution in a timely manner (e.g., review of the QC records).
Participate, as required, in proficiency testing/interpretation/reporting using established procedures and resulting in a satisfactory report.
Promptly verify abnormal/panic results and notify, as required per SOP, patient care unit and/or physician with full documentation of steps taken.
Participate in the educational endeavors of the institution to help meet the current and future needs of the hospital.
Participate, as required, in the training, supervision, and evaluation of new employees, as established by laboratory policies (e.g., section training checklist).
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Able to stand and/or sit for long periods of time.
Visual acuity must not be impaired. Color differentiation is required.
Manual dexterity for instrument operation including microscope.
WORKING ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Noisy environment.
Foul or unpleasant odors.
Perform procedures and operate instrumentation while wearing protective apparel.
May be exposed to virus, disease, and infection from patients and specimens.
SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
Able to use a computer keyboard, monitor and mouse.
Able to communicate verbally, written and electronically with healthcare personnel, families and patients.
Able to use numerous types of laboratory equipment.
Ability to organize and prioritize time and tasks to achieve a well-coordinated work effort and to effectively meet work schedules and deadlines.
cond_0189.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Certified by American Society of Clinical Pathologist (ASCP) or equivalent agency as a Cytotechnologist.
Five (5) years' experience as a Cytotechnologist.
Preferred Requirements
Licensed by the state of [Location masked] within 6 months of employment.

Responsible for overseeing the day-to-day activities of assigned laboratory functions. Responsible for the accurate and timely performance of complex quantitative and/or qualitative analyses. A large part of the role involves working closely and regularly with Pathologists in the review and interpretation of specimens, as well as staying in contact with physicians and laboratory staff throughout the day. Process and screen cytological specimens from various body sites. Recognize abnormal and normal cells and classify findings.
cond_0213.responsibilities:
Coordinate the testing activities of the cytology department, regularly communicating with staff involved in the technical preparation of gynecological and non-gynecological samples for cytological review.
Actively contribute to developing, reviewing, and recommending laboratory procedures, policies, and systems.
Assist with the evaluation of competency of testing personnel. Identify testing personnel training needs and ensure training & education are received as appropriate for lab responsibilities.
Perform and analyze according to SOP, basic and complex diagnostic procedures designed to produce accurate reproducible results to meet the needs of patients, as requested by the physician.
Assist Physicians directly with FNA specimen adequacy determination during patient procedures.
Prepare reagent and solution correctly and accurately to complete necessary testing/requests according to the SOP.
Restock the work area and FNA carts of needed supplies to assist co-workers in the performance of their duties.
Prepare and accession patient specimens, accepting only patient specimens for testing that are properly collected and labeled. Evaluate sufficiency of patient information given with specimens and resolve issues with specimen collection and specimen orders in accordance with established laboratory policies.
Perform required quality assurance and control procedures on a predetermined schedule to ascertain the reliability of reagents and laboratory equipment/instrumentation resulting in timely accurate reproducible test results to ensure quality patient care and complete quality control records legibly and accurately.
Perform required troubleshooting and subsequent appropriate problem resolution, in a timely manner (e.g., review of the QC records).
Participate, as required, in proficiency testing/interpretation/reporting using established procedures and resulting in a satisfactory report.
Promptly verify abnormal/panic results and notify, as required per SOP, patient care unit and/or physician with full documentation of steps taken.
Participate in the educational endeavors of the institution to meet the current and future needs of the hospital.
Participate, as required, in the training, supervision and evaluation of new employees, as established by laboratory policies (e.g., section training checklist).
cond_0213.requirements:
Certified by American Society of Clinical Pathologist (ASCP) or equivalent agency as a Cytotechnologist.
Licensed by the state of [Location masked] within 6 months of employment.
Five (5) years' experience as a Cytotechnologist.
Able to stand and/or sit for long periods of time.
Visual acuity must not be impaired. Color differentiation is required.
Manual dexterity for instrument operation including microscope.
Able to work in a noisy environment with foul or unpleasant odors.
Able to perform procedures and operate instrumentation while wearing protective apparel.
May be exposed to virus, disease, and infection from patients and specimens.
Able to use a computer keyboard, monitor and mouse.
Able to communicate verbally, in writing, and electronically with healthcare personnel, families and patients.
Able to use numerous types of laboratory equipment.
Ability to organize and prioritize time and tasks to achieve a well-coordinated work effort and to effectively meet work schedules and deadlines.
cond_0213.values: We value having a positive impact on the people our work affects. We aim to act with responsibility, fairness, and respect in the way we make decisions and deliver our work.

Process and screen cytological specimens from various body sites. Work in close relationship with Pathologists in review and interpretation of the specimens. Recognize abnormal and normal cells and classify findings.
CORE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Coordinate the testing activities of the cytology department, oversee staff involved in the technical preparation of gynecological and non-gynecological samples for cytological review.
Assist in developing, reviewing, recommending, laboratory procedures, policies, and systems.
Assist with the evaluation of competency of testing personnel. Identify testing personnel training needs and ensure training & education are received as appropriate for lab responsibilities.
Perform and analyze according to SOP, basic and complex diagnostic procedures designed to produce accurate reproducible results to meet the needs of patients, as requested by the physician.
Assist Physicians with FNA specimen adequacy determination during patient procedures.
Prepare, reagent, and solution correctly and accurately to complete necessary testing/requests according to the SOP.
Restock the work area and FNA carts of needed supplies to assist co-workers in the performance of their duties.
Prepare and accession patient specimens, accepting only patient specimens for testing that are properly collected and labeled. Evaluate sufficiency of patient information given with specimens and resolve issues with specimen collection and specimen orders in accordance with established laboratory policies.
Perform required quality assurance and control procedures on a predetermined schedule to ascertain the reliability of reagents and laboratory equipment/instrumentation resulting in timely accurate reproducible test results to ensure quality patient care and complete quality control records legibly and accurately.
Perform required troubleshooting and subsequent appropriate problem resolution, in a timely manner (e.g., review of the QC records).
Participate, as required, in proficiency testing/interpretation/reporting using established procedures and resulting in a satisfactory report.
Promptly verify, abnormal/panic results and notifies, as required per SOP, patient care unit and/or physician with full documentation of steps taken.
Participate in the educational endeavors of the institution to meet the current and future needs of the hospital.
Participate, as required, in the training, supervision and evaluation of new employees, as established by laboratory policies (e.g., section training checklist).
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Able to stand and/or sit for long periods of time.
Visual acuity must not be impaired. Color differentiation is required.
Manual dexterity for instrument operation including microscope.
WORKING ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Noisy environment.
Foul or unpleasant odors.
Perform procedures and operate instrumentation while wearing protective apparel.
May be exposed to virus, disease, and infection from patients and specimens.
SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
Able to use a computer keyboard, monitor and mouse.
Able to communicate verbally, written and electronically with healthcare personnel, families and patients.
Able to use numerous types of laboratory equipment.
Ability to organize and prioritize time and tasks to achieve a well-coordinated work effort and to effectively meet work schedules and deadlines.
cond_0298.requirements:
Certified by American Society of Clinical Pathologist (ASCP) or equivalent agency as a Cytotechnologist.
Licensed by the state of [Location masked] within 6 months of employment.
Five (5) years' experience as a Cytotechnologist.

Process and screen cytological specimens from various body sites. Work in close relationship with Pathologists in review and interpretation of the specimens. Recognize abnormal and normal cells and classify findings.
CORE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Coordinate the testing activities of the cytology department, oversee staff involved in the technical preparation of gynecological and non-gynecological samples for cytological review.
Assist in developing, reviewing, recommending, laboratory procedures, policies, and systems.
Assist with the evaluation of competency of testing personnel. Identify testing personnel training needs and ensure training & education are received as appropriate for lab responsibilities.
Perform and analyze according to SOP, basic and complex diagnostic procedures designed to produce accurate reproducible results to meet the needs of patients, as requested by the physician.
Assist Physicians with FNA specimen adequacy determination during patient procedures.
Prepare, reagent, and solution correctly and accurately to complete necessary testing/requests according to the SOP.
Restock the work area and FNA carts of needed supplies to assist co-workers in the performance of their duties.
Prepare and accession patient specimens, accepting only patient specimens for testing that are properly collected and labeled. Evaluate sufficiency of patient information given with specimens and resolve issues with specimen collection and specimen orders in accordance with established laboratory policies.
Perform required quality assurance and control procedures on a predetermined schedule to ascertain the reliability of reagents and laboratory equipment/instrumentation resulting in timely accurate reproducible test results to ensure quality patient care and complete quality control records legibly and accurately.
Perform required troubleshooting and subsequent appropriate problem resolution, in a timely manner (e.g., review of the QC records).
Participate, as required, in proficiency testing/interpretation/reporting using established procedures and resulting in a satisfactory report.
Promptly verify, abnormal/panic results and notifies, as required per SOP, patient care unit and/or physician with full documentation of steps taken.
Participate in the educational endeavors of the institution to meet the current and future needs of the hospital.
Participate, as required, in the training, supervision and evaluation of new employees, as established by laboratory policies (e.g., section training checklist).
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Able to stand and/or sit for long periods of time.
Visual acuity must not be impaired. Color differentiation is required.
Manual dexterity for instrument operation including microscope.
WORKING ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Noisy environment.
Foul or unpleasant odors.
Perform procedures and operate instrumentation while wearing protective apparel.
May be exposed to virus, disease, and infection from patients and specimens.
SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
Able to use a computer keyboard, monitor and mouse.
Able to communicate verbally, written and electronically with healthcare personnel, families and patients.
Able to use numerous types of laboratory equipment.
Ability to organize and prioritize time and tasks to achieve a well-coordinated work effort and to effectively meet work schedules and deadlines.
cond_0343.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Certified by American Society of Clinical Pathologist (ASCP) or equivalent agency as a Cytotechnologist.
Five (5) years' experience as a Cytotechnologist.
Preferred Requirements
Licensed by the state of [Location masked] within 6 months of employment.

Coordinate the testing activities of the cytology department, oversee staff involved in the technical preparation of gynecological and non-gynecological samples for cytological review.
Assist in developing, reviewing, recommending, laboratory procedures, policies, and systems.
Assist with the evaluation of competency of testing personnel. Identify testing personnel training needs and ensure training & education are received as appropriate for lab responsibilities.
Perform and analyze according to SOP, basic and complex diagnostic procedures designed to produce accurate reproducible results to meet the needs of patients, as requested by the physician.
Assist Physicians with FNA specimen adequacy determination during patient procedures.
Prepare, reagent, and solution correctly and accurately to complete necessary testing/requests according to the SOP.
Restock the work area and FNA carts of needed supplies to assist co-workers in the performance of their duties.
Prepare and accession patient specimens, accepting only patient specimens for testing that are properly collected and labeled. Evaluate sufficiency of patient information given with specimens and resolve issues with specimen collection and specimen orders in accordance with established laboratory policies.
Perform required quality assurance and control procedures on a predetermined schedule to ascertain the reliability of reagents and laboratory equipment/instrumentation resulting in timely accurate reproducible test results to ensure quality patient care and complete quality control records legibly and accurately.
Perform required troubleshooting and subsequent appropriate problem resolution, in a timely manner (e.g., review of the QC records).
Participate, as required, in proficiency testing/interpretation/reporting using established procedures and resulting in a satisfactory report.
Promptly verify, abnormal/panic results and notifies, as required per SOP, patient care unit and/or physician with full documentation of steps taken.
Participate in the educational endeavors of the institution to meet the current and future needs of the hospital.
Participate, as required, in the training, supervision and evaluation of new employees, as established by laboratory policies (e.g., section training checklist).
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Able to stand and/or sit for long periods of time.
Visual acuity must not be impaired. Color differentiation is required.
Manual dexterity for instrument operation including microscope.
WORKING ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Noisy environment.
Foul or unpleasant odors.
Perform procedures and operate instrumentation while wearing protective apparel.
May be exposed to virus, disease, and infection from patients and specimens.
SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
Able to use a computer keyboard, monitor and mouse.
Able to communicate verbally, written and electronically with healthcare personnel, families and patients.
Able to use numerous types of laboratory equipment.
Ability to organize and prioritize time and tasks to achieve a well-coordinated work effort and to effectively meet work schedules and deadlines.
cond_0365.requirements:

Certified by American Society of Clinical Pathologist (ASCP) or equivalent agency as a Cytotechnologist.
Five (5) years' experience as a Cytotechnologist.

cond_0387.intro: We are looking for someone to join our team and help coordinate the day-to-day activities of assigned laboratory functions. This role works closely with Pathologists and laboratory staff to support accurate and timely performance of complex cytological analyses, including processing and screening specimens from various body sites, and contributing to the review and interpretation of findings.
cond_0387.responsibilities:
CORE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Coordinate the testing activities of the cytology department, working alongside staff involved in the technical preparation of gynecological and non-gynecological samples for cytological review.
Collaborate in developing, reviewing, and recommending laboratory procedures, policies, and systems.
Support the evaluation of competency of testing personnel. Help identify training needs and ensure staff receive appropriate training and education for their lab responsibilities.
Perform and analyze according to SOP, basic and complex diagnostic procedures designed to produce accurate reproducible results to meet the needs of patients, as requested by the physician.
Work alongside Physicians to assist with FNA specimen adequacy determination during patient procedures.
Prepare reagents and solutions correctly and accurately to complete necessary testing/requests according to the SOP.
Restock the work area and FNA carts of needed supplies to assist co-workers in the performance of their duties.
Prepare and accession patient specimens, accepting only patient specimens for testing that are properly collected and labeled. Evaluate sufficiency of patient information given with specimens and help resolve issues with specimen collection and specimen orders in accordance with established laboratory policies.
Carry out required quality assurance and control procedures on a predetermined schedule to support the reliability of reagents and laboratory equipment/instrumentation, and complete quality control records legibly and accurately.
Perform required troubleshooting and coordinate appropriate problem resolution in a timely manner (e.g., review of the QC records).
Participate, as required, in proficiency testing/interpretation/reporting using established procedures and resulting in a satisfactory report.
Promptly verify abnormal/panic results and notify, as required per SOP, patient care unit and/or physician with full documentation of steps taken.
Participate in the educational endeavors of the institution to help meet the current and future needs of the hospital.
Participate, as required, in the training, supervision, and evaluation of new employees, as established by laboratory policies (e.g., section training checklist).
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Able to stand and/or sit for long periods of time.
Visual acuity must not be impaired. Color differentiation is required.
Manual dexterity for instrument operation including microscope.
WORKING ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Noisy environment.
Foul or unpleasant odors.
Perform procedures and operate instrumentation while wearing protective apparel.
May be exposed to virus, disease, and infection from patients and specimens.
SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
Able to use a computer keyboard, monitor and mouse.
Able to communicate verbally, written and electronically with healthcare personnel, families and patients.
Able to use numerous types of laboratory equipment.
Ability to organize and prioritize time and tasks to achieve a well-coordinated work effort and to effectively meet work schedules and deadlines.
cond_0387.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Certified by American Society of Clinical Pathologist (ASCP) or equivalent agency as a Cytotechnologist.
Five (5) years' experience as a Cytotechnologist.
Preferred Requirements
Licensed by the state of [Location masked] within 6 months of employment.

cond_0463.intro: We are looking for someone to join our team in this role. Responsible for overseeing the day-to-day activities of assigned laboratory functions. Responsible for the accurate and timely performance of complex quantitative and/or qualitative analyses. Process and screen cytological specimens from various body sites. Work in close relationship with Pathologists in review and interpretation of the specimens. Recognize abnormal and normal cells and classify findings. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of cytological analysis and specimen interpretation.
cond_0463.responsibilities:
CORE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Coordinate the testing activities of the cytology department, oversee staff involved in the technical preparation of gynecological and non-gynecological samples for cytological review.
Assist in developing, reviewing, recommending, laboratory procedures, policies, and systems.
Assist with the evaluation of competency of testing personnel. Identify testing personnel training needs and ensure training & education are received as appropriate for lab responsibilities.
Perform and analyze according to SOP, basic and complex diagnostic procedures designed to produce accurate reproducible results to meet the needs of patients, as requested by the physician.
Assist Physicians with FNA specimen adequacy determination during patient procedures.
Prepare, reagent, and solution correctly and accurately to complete necessary testing/requests according to the SOP.
Restock the work area and FNA carts of needed supplies to assist co-workers in the performance of their duties.
Prepare and accession patient specimens, accepting only patient specimens for testing that are properly collected and labeled. Evaluate sufficiency of patient information given with specimens and resolve issues with specimen collection and specimen orders in accordance with established laboratory policies.
Perform required quality assurance and control procedures on a predetermined schedule to ascertain the reliability of reagents and laboratory equipment/instrumentation resulting in timely accurate reproducible test results to ensure quality patient care and complete quality control records legibly and accurately.
Perform required troubleshooting and subsequent appropriate problem resolution, in a timely manner (e.g., review of the QC records).
Participate, as required, in proficiency testing/interpretation/reporting using established procedures and resulting in a satisfactory report.
Promptly verify, abnormal/panic results and notifies, as required per SOP, patient care unit and/or physician with full documentation of steps taken.
Participate in the educational endeavors of the institution to meet the current and future needs of the hospital.
Participate, as required, in the training, supervision and evaluation of new employees, as established by laboratory policies (e.g., section training checklist).
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Able to stand and/or sit for long periods of time.
Visual acuity must not be impaired. Color differentiation is required.
Manual dexterity for instrument operation including microscope.
WORKING ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Noisy environment.
Foul or unpleasant odors.
Perform procedures and operate instrumentation while wearing protective apparel.
May be exposed to virus, disease, and infection from patients and specimens.
SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
Able to use a computer keyboard, monitor and mouse.
Able to communicate verbally, written and electronically with healthcare personnel, families and patients.
Able to use numerous types of laboratory equipment.
Ability to organize and prioritize time and tasks to achieve a well-coordinated work effort and to effectively meet work schedules and deadlines.
cond_0463.requirements:
Certified by American Society of Clinical Pathologist (ASCP) or equivalent agency as a Cytotechnologist.
Licensed by the state of [Location masked] within 6 months of employment.
Five (5) years' experience as a Cytotechnologist.

This role works closely with Pathologists and laboratory staff to support accurate and timely performance of complex cytological analyses, including processing and screening specimens from various body sites, and contributing to the review and interpretation of findings.
cond_0522.responsibilities:
CORE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Coordinate the testing activities of the cytology department, working alongside staff involved in the technical preparation of gynecological and non-gynecological samples for cytological review.
Collaborate on developing, reviewing, and recommending laboratory procedures, policies, and systems.
Support the evaluation of competency of testing personnel. Help identify training needs and ensure training and education are received as appropriate for lab responsibilities.
Perform and analyze according to SOP, basic and complex diagnostic procedures designed to produce accurate reproducible results to meet the needs of patients, as requested by the physician.
Work with Physicians to assist with FNA specimen adequacy determination during patient procedures.
Prepare reagent and solution correctly and accurately to complete necessary testing/requests according to the SOP.
Restock the work area and FNA carts of needed supplies to assist co-workers in the performance of their duties.
Prepare and accession patient specimens, accepting only patient specimens for testing that are properly collected and labeled. Evaluate sufficiency of patient information given with specimens and resolve issues with specimen collection and specimen orders in accordance with established laboratory policies.
Perform required quality assurance and control procedures on a predetermined schedule to ascertain the reliability of reagents and laboratory equipment/instrumentation resulting in timely accurate reproducible test results to ensure quality patient care and complete quality control records legibly and accurately.
Perform required troubleshooting and subsequent appropriate problem resolution, in a timely manner (e.g., review of the QC records).
Participate, as required, in proficiency testing/interpretation/reporting using established procedures and resulting in a satisfactory report.
Promptly verify abnormal/panic results and notify, as required per SOP, patient care unit and/or physician with full documentation of steps taken.
Participate in the educational endeavors of the institution to meet the current and future needs of the hospital.
Participate, as required, in the training, supervision and evaluation of new employees, as established by laboratory policies (e.g., section training checklist).
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Able to stand and/or sit for long periods of time.
Visual acuity must not be impaired. Color differentiation is required.
Manual dexterity for instrument operation including microscope.
WORKING ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Noisy environment.
Foul or unpleasant odors.
Perform procedures and operate instrumentation while wearing protective apparel.
May be exposed to virus, disease, and infection from patients and specimens.
SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
Able to use a computer keyboard, monitor and mouse.
Able to communicate verbally, written and electronically with healthcare personnel, families and patients.
Able to use numerous types of laboratory equipment.
Ability to organize and prioritize time and tasks to achieve a well-coordinated work effort and to effectively meet work schedules and deadlines.
cond_0522.requirements:
Certified by American Society of Clinical Pathologist (ASCP) or equivalent agency as a Cytotechnologist.
Licensed by the state of [Location masked] within 6 months of employment.
Five (5) years' experience as a Cytotechnologist.

Responsible for overseeing the day-to-day activities of assigned laboratory functions. Responsible for the accurate and timely performance of complex quantitative and/or qualitative analyses. Process and screen cytological specimens from various body sites. Coordinate with Pathologists on review and interpretation of specimens. Recognize abnormal and normal cells and classify findings.
cond_0538.responsibilities:
The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Coordinate the testing activities of the cytology department; oversee staff involved in the technical preparation of gynecological and non-gynecological samples for cytological review.
Assist in developing, reviewing, and recommending laboratory procedures, policies, and systems.
Assist with the evaluation of competency of testing personnel. Identify testing personnel training needs and ensure training and education are received as appropriate for lab responsibilities.
Perform and analyze according to SOP, basic and complex diagnostic procedures designed to produce accurate reproducible results to meet the needs of patients, as requested by the physician.
Assist Physicians with FNA specimen adequacy determination during patient procedures.
Prepare reagents and solutions correctly and accurately to complete necessary testing/requests according to the SOP.
Restock the work area and FNA carts with needed supplies to support co-workers in the performance of their duties.
Prepare and accession patient specimens, accepting only specimens that are properly collected and labeled. Evaluate sufficiency of patient information given with specimens and resolve issues with specimen collection and orders in accordance with established laboratory policies.
Perform required quality assurance and control procedures on a predetermined schedule to verify the reliability of reagents and laboratory equipment/instrumentation, resulting in timely accurate reproducible test results; complete quality control records legibly and accurately.
Perform required troubleshooting and subsequent appropriate problem resolution in a timely manner (e.g., review of QC records).
Participate, as required, in proficiency testing/interpretation/reporting using established procedures, resulting in a satisfactory report.
Promptly verify abnormal/panic results and notify, as required per SOP, the patient care unit and/or physician, with full documentation of steps taken.
Participate in the educational endeavors of the institution to meet the current and future needs of the hospital.
Participate, as required, in the training, supervision, and evaluation of new employees, as established by laboratory policies (e.g., section training checklist).
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Able to stand and/or sit for long periods of time.
Visual acuity must not be impaired. Color differentiation is required.
Manual dexterity for instrument operation including microscope.
WORKING ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Noisy environment.
Foul or unpleasant odors.
Perform procedures and operate instrumentation while wearing protective apparel.
May be exposed to virus, disease, and infection from patients and specimens.
cond_0538.requirements:
Certified by American Society of Clinical Pathologist (ASCP) or equivalent agency as a Cytotechnologist.
Licensed by the state of [Location masked] within 6 months of employment.
Five (5) years' experience as a Cytotechnologist.
Able to use a computer keyboard, monitor and mouse.
Able to communicate verbally, in writing, and electronically with healthcare personnel, families, and patients.
Able to use numerous types of laboratory equipment.
Ability to organize and prioritize time and tasks to achieve a well-coordinated work effort and to effectively meet work schedules and deadlines.

Coordinate the testing activities of the cytology department, working alongside staff involved in the technical preparation of gynecological and non-gynecological samples for cytological review.
Collaborate in developing, reviewing, and recommending laboratory procedures, policies, and systems.
Support the evaluation of competency of testing personnel. Help identify training needs and ensure staff receive appropriate training and education for their lab responsibilities.
Perform and analyze according to SOP, basic and complex diagnostic procedures designed to produce accurate reproducible results to meet the needs of patients, as requested by the physician.
Work alongside Physicians to assist with FNA specimen adequacy determination during patient procedures.
Prepare reagents and solutions correctly and accurately to complete necessary testing/requests according to the SOP.
Restock the work area and FNA carts of needed supplies to assist co-workers in the performance of their duties.
Prepare and accession patient specimens, accepting only patient specimens for testing that are properly collected and labeled. Evaluate sufficiency of patient information given with specimens and help resolve issues with specimen collection and specimen orders in accordance with established laboratory policies.
Carry out required quality assurance and control procedures on a predetermined schedule to support the reliability of reagents and laboratory equipment/instrumentation, and complete quality control records legibly and accurately.
Perform required troubleshooting and coordinate appropriate problem resolution in a timely manner (e.g., review of the QC records).
Participate, as required, in proficiency testing/interpretation/reporting using established procedures and resulting in a satisfactory report.
Promptly verify abnormal/panic results and notify, as required per SOP, patient care unit and/or physician with full documentation of steps taken.
Participate in the educational endeavors of the institution to help meet the current and future needs of the hospital.
Participate, as required, in the training, supervision, and evaluation of new employees, as established by laboratory policies (e.g., section training checklist).
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Able to stand and/or sit for long periods of time.
Visual acuity must not be impaired. Color differentiation is required.
Manual dexterity for instrument operation including microscope.
WORKING ENVIRONMENT: The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Noisy environment.
Foul or unpleasant odors.
Perform procedures and operate instrumentation while wearing protective apparel.
May be exposed to virus, disease, and infection from patients and specimens.
SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
Able to use a computer keyboard, monitor and mouse.
Able to communicate verbally, written and electronically with healthcare personnel, families and patients.
Able to use numerous types of laboratory equipment.
Ability to organize and prioritize time and tasks to achieve a well-coordinated work effort and to effectively meet work schedules and deadlines.

cond_0648.intro: We are looking for someone to join our team and help coordinate the day-to-day activities of assigned laboratory functions. This role works closely with Pathologists and laboratory staff to support accurate and timely performance of complex cytological analyses, including processing and screening specimens from various body sites, and contributing to the review and interpretation of findings.
cond_0648.responsibilities:
CORE DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: The statements described here are intended to describe the general nature of work being performed by people assigned to this position. They are not intended to be constructed as an all-inclusive list of all responsibilities and duties. Other duties may be assigned.
Coordinate the testing activities of the cytology department, working alongside staff involved in the technical preparation of gynecological and non-gynecological samples for cytological review.
Collaborate on developing, reviewing, and recommending laboratory procedures, policies, and systems.
Support the evaluation of competency of testing personnel. Help identify training needs and ensure training and education are received as appropriate for lab responsibilities.
Perform and analyze according to SOP, basic and complex diagnostic procedures designed to produce accurate reproducible results to meet the needs of patients, as requested by the physician.
Work with Physicians to assist with FNA specimen adequacy determination during patient procedures.
Prepare reagent and solution correctly and accurately to complete necessary testing/requests according to the SOP.
Restock the work area and FNA carts of needed supplies to assist co-workers in the performance of their duties.
Prepare and accession patient specimens, accepting only patient specimens for testing that are properly collected and labeled. Evaluate sufficiency of patient information given with specimens and resolve issues with specimen collection and specimen orders in accordance with established laboratory policies.
Perform required quality assurance and control procedures on a predetermined schedule to ascertain the reliability of reagents and laboratory equipment/instrumentation resulting in timely accurate reproducible test results to ensure quality patient care and complete quality control records legibly and accurately.
Perform required troubleshooting and subsequent appropriate problem resolution, in a timely manner (e.g., review of the QC records).
Participate, as required, in proficiency testing/interpretation/reporting using established procedures and resulting in a satisfactory report.
Promptly verify abnormal/panic results and notify, as required per SOP, patient care unit and/or physician with full documentation of steps taken.
Participate in the educational endeavors of the institution to meet the current and future needs of the hospital.
Participate, as required, in the training, supervision and evaluation of new employees, as established by laboratory policies (e.g., section training checklist).
